section.title: Middleware Integration
section.p: The actual added value of the DOG framework is it integration in all major middleware standards. The framework works transparently with CORBA, RMI, and J2EE. The persistency layer OJB provides integration with all major database systems.

section.title: DOG Origins
section.p: The ancestor of the DOG framework is a C++ framework which development started 1995. The name of the framework was "Impendance Mismatch". The framework was used in several industrial projects developed in C++/C for telecommunications and industrial controls companies. At the same time tha application framework was designed to initialize complex embedded telecommunication devices.

The framework ideas were used to develop a new framework in Java. New features such as reflection were used and solutions were found to replace templates and function pointers. This framework was developed at the end of last millenium. It was named SOODBM - Simple Object-Oriented DataBase Management -. A first version of the explorer framework was written to visualize the data stored in the SOODBM. This visualization framework evolved to the actual application and explorer packages.

All these frameworks were released under open source licenses and freely distributed to interested parties. The customers paid us to integrate the framework and help them define the architectur of their products and not for the frameworks.

section.p: The source distribution of the project contains a release note document. The major changes and error corrections for each release are documented there.
